G6401:
ἀπαράλλακτος [παραλλάσσω]
unchanged, unchangeable, Plut.
G6404:
ἀπάρχομαι
Dep.
I. to make a beginning, esp. in sacrifice, τρίχας ἀπάρχεσθαι to begin the sacrifice with the hair, i. e. by cutting off the hair from the forehead and throwing it into the fire, Il.: to begin the sacrificial rites, Od.
II. c. gen. to cut off part of a thing, to offer it, to offer part of a thing, Hdt., Eur.
III. to offer the firstlings or first-fruits, Hdt., Ar.
2. metaph. to take as the first-fruits, as the choice or best, Theocr.
IV. ἀπάρχω Act., to be the first, be leader, dance, Anth.
G6407:
ἀπελευθερόω [from ἀπελεύθερος]
to emancipate a slave, Plat.
G6409:
ἀπερείδω
I. to rest, fix, settle, τὴν ὄψιν πρός τι Luc.
2. intr. = Pass. to rest upon, id.
II. mostly as Pass., with fut. and aor1 mid., to support oneself upon, rest upon a thing, c. dat., Xen., etc.; εἴς τι Plat.
G6411:
ἀπηλιώτης [ἥλιος]
the wind that comes from the rising sun, the east wind, Lat. subsolanus, Hdt., Thuc.
G6412:
ἄπιος
a pear-tree, Lat. pirus, Arist.

ἄπιος [The first sense has short α, the latter α—.] [ἀπό]
I. far away, far off, distant, ἐξ ἀπίης γαίης Hom.
II. Ἄπιος, η, ον, Apian, i. e. Peloponnesian (said to be derived from Ἆπις, a king of Argos), Ἀπία γῆ, Ἀπία χθών, or Ἀπία alone, the Peloponnese, esp. Argolis, Aesch., Soph.; so Ἀπίς, ίδος, ἡ, Theocr.
G6413:
ἄπλαστος
not moulded, i. e. in its natural state, natural, unaffected, Plut.
G6414:
ἄπληστος [πίμπλημι]
I. not to be filled, insatiate, Soph., etc.
2. c. gen., ἄπλ. χρημάτων insatiate of money, Hdt., etc.
II. adv., ἀπλήστως ἔχειν to be insatiate, Plat.; ἀπλ. διακεῖσθαι or ἔχειν πρός τι Xen.
G6416:
ἁπλόω [ἁπλοῦς]
to make single, to unfold, stretch out, Batr., Anth.:—Pass., ἡπλώθη [the fish] lay stretched out, Babr.
G6417:
ἀποβιάζομαι
I. Dep. to force away:— Pass. to be forced away or back, Xen.
II. absol. to use force, id.
G6419:
ἀπόγονος [ἀπογίγνομαι]
born or descended from, Lat. oriundus, Hdt.: in pl. descendants, id., Thuc.; ἀπόγονοι τεαί thy offspring, Soph.
G6421:
ἀπόδεσμος
I. a breastband, girdle, Luc.
II. a bundle, bunch, Plut.
G6422:
ἀποδέω
to bind fast, Plat.

ἀποδέω
to be in want of, lack, τριακοσίων ἀποδέοντα μύρια 10, 000 lacking 300, Thuc.: to fall short of, be inferior to, τινός Luc.
G6424:
ἀποδιδράσκω
1. to run away or off, escape, or flee from, esp. by stealth, Od., Hdt., attic; of runaway slaves, Xen.; of soldiers, to desert, id.
2. c. acc. to flee, shun, Hdt., Thuc.
G6425:
ἀποδιώκω
to chase away, Thuc.; οὐκ ἀποδιώξει σαυτόν; i. e. take yourself off, Ar.
G6427:
ἀπόδοσις [ἀποδίδωμι]
1. a giving back, restitution, return, τινος of a thing, Hdt., attic
2. payment, τοῦ μισθοῦ Thuc.
G6428:
ἀποθερίζω
to cut off, κόμας Eur.
G6430:
ἀποικία [ἄποικος]
a settlement far from home, a colony settlement, Hdt., etc.; εἰς ἀπ. στέλλειν to send away so as to form a settlement, id.; ἀπ. ἐκπέμπειν Thuc.
G6432:
ἀποικισμός
the settlement of a colony, Arist.
G6433:
ἀποίχομαι
1. to be gone away, to be far from, c. gen., Il., attic
2. absol. to be gone, to have departed, to be absent, Od.: hence, to be gone, to have perished, ἀποίχεται χάρις Eur.: of persons, to be dead and gone, Pind., Ar.
G6434:
ἀποκαθαίρω
I. to cleanse or clean quite, ἀπ. τὴν χεῖρα εἰς τὰ χειρόμακτρα upon the towels, Xen.
2. to refine from dross, Strab.: metaph. in Pass., ἀποκεκαθάρθαι τὴν φωνήν to be pure in dialect, Luc.
II. to clear away, τὰς τραπέζας Ar.:—Mid., ἀποκαθήρασθαί τινος to rid oneself of a thing, Xen.
G6436:
ἀποκάθημαι
Pass. to sit apart, ἀτιμώμενοι ἀποκατέαται (ionic for ‐κάθηνται) Hdt.
G6438:
ἀποκαλέω
I. to call back, recall, from exile, Hdt., Xen.
2. to call away or aside, Xen.
II. to call by a name, esp. by way of disparagement, to stigmatise as, τὸν τοῦ μανέντος ξύναιμον ἀποκαλοῦντες Soph.; σοφιστὴν ἀπ. τινα Xen.
G6442:
ἀποικίζω
I. to send away from home, Od., Soph., etc.:—Pass. to be settled in a far land, to emigrate, Plat.
II. to colonise a place, send a colony to it, c. acc., Hdt., Thuc.
G6443:
ἀποκλαίω
I. to weep aloud, Hdt.; c. acc. cogn., ἀπ. στόνον Soph.
2. ἀπ. τινα or τι to bewail much, mourn deeply for, Aesch., Plat.; so in Mid., ἀποκλαίεσθαι κακά Soph.; τὴν πενίαν Ar.
II. Mid., also, to cease to wail, Luc.
G6445:
ἀποκλίνω
I. to turn off or aside, τι Od.: to turn back, Hhymn.:—Pass., of the day, to decline, get towards evening, Hdt.
II. Pass. to be upset, Dem.
III. intr. in Act. to turn aside or off the road, Xen.; πρὸς τὴν ἠῶ ἀποκλίνοντι as one turns to go Eastward, Hdt.
2. often in bad sense, to fall away, decline, degenerate, Soph.; ἐπὶ τὸ ῥαιθυμεῖν Dem.:—and without bad sense, to have a leaning, be favourably disposed, πρός τινα id.
G6446:
ἀποκλύζω
to wash away: metaph. in Mid. to purge, Plat.: to avert by purifications, Ar.
G6447:
ἀποκνίζω
to nip off.
G6448:
ἀποκομίζω
to carry away, escort, Xen.: to carry away captive, Thuc.:—Pass. to take oneself off, get away, id.: to return, Hdt.
G6451:
ἀποκωλύω
I. to hinder or prevent from a thing, τινά τινος Xen.; c. inf., ἀπ. τινὰ ποιεῖν to prevent from doing, forbid to do, μὴ ποιεῖν τι Eur., Xen.
II. c. acc. only, to keep off, hinder, Orac. ap. Hdt., Thuc.: —absol. to stop the way, Thuc.:—impers., οὐδὲν ἀποκωλύει there is no hindrance, Plat.
G6453:
ἀπολακτίζω
1. to kick off or away, shake off, ὕπνον Aesch.
2. to spurn, id.
G6454:
ἀπολαύω
1. to have enjoyment of a thing, to have the benefit of it, to enjoy, c. gen., Hdt., attic:—with acc. added, ἀπολαύειν τί τινος to enjoy an advantage from some source, Ar., Thuc.
2. ironically, to have the benefit of, τῶν Οἰδίπου κακῶν Eur.: —absol. to have a benefit, come finely off, Ar.
G6455:
ἀπολέγω
to pick out from a number, to pick out, choose, Hdt.:—Mid. to pick out for oneself, id., Thuc.; ἀπολελεγμένοι, attic ‐ειλεγμένοι, picked men, Hdt., Xen.

ἀπολέγω
like ἀπαγορεύω, to decline, refuse: — Mid. to decline something offered to one, renounce, Plut.:—absol. to give in, id.
G6457:
ἀπολόγημα [from ἀπολογέομαι]
a plea alleged in defence, Plut.
G6459:
ἀπολυτρόω
to release on payment of ransom, c. gen. pretii, Philipp. ap. Dem.
G6461:
ἀποξενόω [from ἀπόξενος]
to drive from house and home, banish, Plut.:—Pass., γῆς ἀποξενοῦσθαι Eur.
G6462:
ἀποξηραίνω
1. to dry up a river, Hdt.:—Pass. to be dried up, run dry, of rivers, id.
2. generally to dry completely, τὰς ναῦς Thuc.
G6463:
ἀποξύω
to strip off as it were a skin, Il.
G6464:
ἀποπειράομαι
to make trial, essay, or proof of a thing or person, c. gen., Hdt., attic:—so also in Act., ἀποπειρᾶσαι τοῦ Πειραιῶς to make an attempt on the Peiraeeus, Thuc.
G6466:
ἀποπηδάω
1. to leap off from, ἵππου Plut.
2. to start off from, turn away from, τινός Xen.
3. absol. to leap off, start off, Plat.
G6471:
ἀποπομπή [ἀποπέμπω]
a sending away: getting rid of an illness, Luc.
G6472:
ἀπορρέω
I. to flow or run off, stream forth, Hdt., Aesch.; ἀπό τινος Hdt.; ἔκ τινος Plat.
II. to fall off, as fruit, feathers, leaves, etc., Hdt., attic
2. to die away, fade from remembrance, Soph.
G6475:
ἀποσβέννυμι
I. to put out, extinguish, quench, Ar., Plat., etc.
II. Pass., with fut. mid. aor2 and perf. act. intr., and aor1 pass.— to be extinguished, go out, cease to exist, Eur., Xen.
G6476:
ἀποσείω
to shake off:— Mid. to shake off from oneself, Theogn.; of a horse, to throw his rider, Hdt., Xen.; metaph., ἀποσείεσθαι λύπην Ar.
G6477:
ἀποσιωπάω
I. to cease speaking, maintain silence, Isocr., Plut.
II. trans. to keep secret, Luc.
G6479:
ἀποσκηνόω [From ἀπόσκηνος]
I. to keep apart from, Plut.
II. = ἀποσκηνέω, id.
G6484:
ἀποσοβέω
I. to scare away, as one does birds or flies, Ar.; metaph., ἀποσοβῆσαι τὸν γέλων id.
II. intr. to be off in a hurry, οὐκ ἀποσοβήσεις; i. e. be off! id.
G6485:
ἀπόσπασμα [From ἀποσπάω]
that which is torn off, a piece, rag, shred, Plat.
G6486:
ἀποστάζω
I. to let fall drop by drop, distil, Theocr.
II. intr. to fall in drops, distil, Soph.
G6488:
ἀπόστασις [ἀφίσταμαι]
a standing away from, and so,
1. a defection, revolt, ἀπό τινος or τινος Hdt., Thuc.; πρός τινα Thuc.
2. departure from, βίου Eur.
3. distance, interval, Plat.
G6489:
ἀποστατέω [ἀφίσταμαι]
I. to stand aloof from, depart from, be far from, c. gen., Aesch., Soph.; ἀπ. φίλων to fall off from one's friends, Ar.
II. absol. to stand aloof or afar off, Aesch.
G6490:
ἀποστάτης [ἀφίσταμαι]
a runaway slave: a deserter, rebel, Plut.
G6492:
ἀποστέργω
to love no more, Theocr.:—hence to put away from one, reject, Lat. abominari, Aesch.
G6493:
ἀποστροφή [ἀποστρέφομαι]
I. a turning back, Xen.; ἀποστροφὴν λαμβάνειν to have one's course turned, Plut.
II. a turning away from, an escape from a thing, c. gen., Aesch., Eur.
2. a resort, resource, Hdt.:—c. gen. objecti, ὕδατος ἀπ. a resource or means for getting water, id.; σωτηρίας ἀπ. Thuc.
G6495:
ἀποσυρίζω
to whistle aloud for want of thought, Hhymn.:—Pass. to sound like whistling, Luc.
G6496:
ἀποσφραγίζω
to seal up, Plut.:—so in Mid., Eur.
G6498:
ἀποσχίζω
1. to split or cleave off, Od., Eur.
2. to sever or detach from, τινὰ ἀπό τινος Hdt.:—Pass., ἀποσχισθῆναί τινος to be separated from . . ., id.; of a river, to be parted from the main stream, id.; of a tribe, to be detached from its parent stock, id.
3. metaph., ἀπ. τινὰ τοῦ λόγου to cut him off from his speech, interrupt him in it, Ar.
G6499:
ἀποτείνω
1. to stretch out, extend— Pass., Xen.
2. to lengthen, extend, prolong, of the line of an army, id.; of speeches, ἀπ. τὸν λόγον Plat.
